subject: Clarify ledger treatment for promo top-up & trial extension
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: $10k promo top-up + 30d trial extension for BlueNectar (DN-2025-0421)

Irene / Finance team —

BlueNectar (Alan Brooks) asked if we can add a $10,000 promotional top-up to their pilot and push their trial end date out by 30 days. Quick background: they signed a PO but billing hasn't yet issued the first invoice (we were waiting on SSO setup). Sales wants the top-up applied immediately so they can run the extended tests.

Ask to Finance: what is the recommended accounting treatment? Two options we discussed internally:
- Issue a credit memo tied to the PO and net it against future billing, or
- Apply an invoice-offset (no standalone credit memo) once the first invoice posts.

Also need the GLA to use, whether this is contra-revenue or an allowance account, and whether any rev-rec change/approval is required for a $10k amount. Deal ID DN-2025-0421.

Attached: proposed addendum (will send once signed).

Next steps: can Finance advise preferred path and any docs you need from Legal/Sales?

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0199

Laura —
Looping you in for accounting guidance. Context copied below from Aditya. BlueNectar wants the credit applied now and a 30-day extension; they already returned a signed addendum (attached). Sales prefers an invoice-offset if possible to keep AR clean, but open to a credit memo if that’s the right control.

Questions for accounting:
1) If we issue a credit memo, which GLA should we post to? (promo discount vs allowance).
2) If we do an invoice-offset in the billing system, what journal entries will finance need to record?
3) Any approval threshold or tax considerations we should surface to the customer?

Attached the signed addendum from BlueNectar.

Thanks —
Irene

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jan 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Clarify ledger treatment for promo top-up & trial extension (DN-2025-0421)

Thanks for the context — read the addendum. Recommendation from Accounting: issue a credit memo (internal CM) for $10,000 that references the contract amendment and the HubSpot deal DN-2025-0421. Reasoning: credit memos give us an auditable AR adjustment with clear linkage to the contract change. If the customer has no posted invoice yet, we can alternatively apply an invoice-offset in the billing system, but we need to create an accounting document behind the scenes so Finance can map it in the ERP.

GLA guidance:
- Use G/L account: 7090 Promotional Discounts (contra-revenue)
- Subsidiary/segment: US-Billing

Journal entry example (high level):
- Debit: Promotional Discounts (7090) $10,000
- Credit: Accounts Receivable $10,000 (or contra AR clearing if applied as offset)

Tax/timing: promotional credits are generally non-taxable reductions to revenue in US, but confirm with Tax if customer in a different jurisdiction. Also note that any credit > $5,000 requires manager sign-off per policy — Laura (me) will approve but will run this by Finance Manager if there's any deviation.

I attached the credit memo template and a sample JE CSV you can hand to ERP. If RevOps wants to do an invoice-offset instead, RevOps should flag the Billing record ID and our team will post the corresponding JE.

Attachments: credit_memo_template.pdf, JE_example.csv

Laura Bennett
Senior Accountant, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: credit_memo_template.pdf (attachment stub); JE_example.csv (attachment stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Clarify ledger treatment for promo top-up & trial extension (DN-2025-0421)

Agree with Laura that a credit memo is clean, but from an Ops standpoint we'd prefer invoicing offset if the first invoice hasn't posted yet — avoids creating an AR adjustment record that we'll immediately zero out. If Finance can accept an offset workflow (i.e., Billing sets offset=true and Finance posts the JE as contra-revenue), RevOps will apply the top-up and extend the trial in the system today.

Action items I can own:
- Provide Billing record ID once top-up is applied
- Coordinate with Finance to ensure JE maps to 7090 and references DN-2025-0421

If you confirm no tax issues, I'll proceed to apply offset on Monday morning.

Karthik
RevOps Manager 
Redwood Inference
